name: Startup Guys

sources.title: Submit Startup page — paid 'startup promotion packages': Basic $49, Standard $99, Premium $349; reviews published in 7-10 working days; claimed stats 80k monthly pageviews, 8k newsletter subs

requirements: Payment required — no free submission option is offered on the page
Tiers: Basic $49 (350+ word review, social share, 5k push subscribers); Standard $99 (500+ word review + 8k newsletter send); Premium $349 (adds promo video + send to '1000+ investors')
The deliverable is a sponsored review article, not a directory listing
preparation: Startup description and key facts — they write the review, but accurate source material helps
Payment method (the page embeds a payment dropdown in USD)
For Premium: willingness to have them produce a promo video
workflow: Select a package in the payment dropdown ($49/$99/$349)
Pay, then supply the startup details they request
Review is published in 7-10 working days per the page
watchFor: This is pay-for-coverage — a purchased review, not earned media; the resulting article is effectively sponsored content
Audience claims (80k pageviews/mo, 8k newsletter, 75k social followers) are self-reported and unverified
'Sent to 1000+ investors' on Premium is a marketing claim — no investor list is evidenced
No free route exists; if zero-cost coverage matters, skip this destination entirely
Site is a WordPress blog; pricing labels are inconsistent ('Standard $49 / Plus $99 / Pro $349' in dropdown vs Basic/Standard/Premium headings)
countsAsLive: A review article about the startup is published on startupguys.net under the Startup Spotlight category
unknowns: Actual traffic/subscriber numbers behind the claimed stats
Whether purchased reviews are labeled as sponsored (paid placement disclosure)
Refund policy if the review never publishes
